title: My Jesus, I Love Thee
description: My Jesus, I Love Thee in Tonic Solfa to GORDON: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the four verses, and a piano.
about: William Ralph Featherstone wrote these words as a young man; Adoniram J. Gordon found them in a London hymnal of 1870 and wrote the tune GORDON for them in 1876.
underlay: My Je-sus, I love_ Thee, I know Thou art mine; For Thee all the fol_-lies of sin I re-sign; My gra-cious Re-deem-er_, my Sa_-vior art Thou_; If ev-er I loved_ Thee, my Je_-sus, ’tis now.

lines: My Jesus, I love Thee, I know Thou art mine;
For Thee all the follies of sin I resign;
My gracious Redeemer, my Savior art Thou;
If ever I loved Thee, my Jesus, ’tis now.
I love Thee because Thou hast first loved me,
And purchased my pardon on Calvary’s tree;
I love Thee for wearing the thorns on Thy brow;
If ever I loved Thee, my Jesus, ’tis now.
I’ll love Thee in life, I will love Thee in death,
And praise Thee as long as Thou lendest me breath;
And say when the death dew lies cold on my brow,
If ever I loved Thee, my Jesus, ’tis now.
In mansions of glory and endless delight,
I’ll ever adore Thee in heaven so bright;
I’ll sing with the glittering crown on my brow,
If ever I loved Thee, my Jesus, ’tis now.
